Proposition
[Ricci flow preserves two-nonnegative curvature] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0137, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0138 ↗ prop:chow-ii-curvature-operator-evolution ↗ prop:chow-ii-ode-preserves-two-nonnegative 1. ch11:11.44\group Ricci Flow Maximum Principles A complete bounded-curvature Ricci flow whose initial curvature operator is two-nonnegative has two-nonnegative curvature operator at every later time.
Proof

\sketch Uhlenbeck’s bundle identification converts the curvature equation into $(\partial _t-\Delta )\operatorname {Rm}=Q(\operatorname {Rm})$. The fiberwise cone corresponding to $\mathcal C$ is closed, convex, invariant under parallel translation, and, by 2, invariant under the reaction ODE. The tensor maximum principle therefore keeps $\operatorname {Rm}$ in this cone for all later times.

□
